opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee without the Payroll Specialist role, admin is not permitted; maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E002 is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as HR noted. Contractors are never admin; with basic training max is read. Admin requested is above max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. HR's database (authoritative for employment type) shows she is a full-time Analyst. Per policy, full-time employees are allowed up to write, and admin is only permitted if the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll, so admin is above the maximum. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), I grant the maximum allowed level: write. (Security's note conflicts on employment type, but even under either interpretation admin is never allowed; HR's record governs employment status, capping access at write.)
